plan_title: Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan Aker Gas Injection No. 1 Freestone County, Texas
ama_definition: The plan constructs the AMA as the year-12 end-of-injection plume plus a half-mile buffer overlain with the year-17 plume (6,417 acres), but then sets the AMA equal to the MMA because the difference is small (p55-56).
mma_definition: The modeled free-phase plume after a 12-year injection period and 25 years of post-injection drift (stabilized when areal growth falls below 0.25% per year) plus a half-mile buffer, about 8,364 acres (p24, p55-56).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Surface equipment (pipeline flanges, valves, wellhead) is the only pathway rated 'possible' during injection; existing wells (27 of 35 penetrate the Eagle Ford in the MMA, 7 within the stabilized plume), future wells, faults, confining zones and seismicity are all rated low likelihood and low magnitude (p57-59, p64-66).
baseline_summary: Pre-plan environmental and operational baselines: soil gas at selected UCZ penetrations, groundwater from well 3907403, atmospheric H2S/CO2 near the facility, and a snapshot of well pressures (wellhead, annular, possibly bottomhole) taken before injection under the plan; baseline surveys reported completed July 2025 with analysis still pending. Thereafter SCADA normal operating ranges serve as the reference (p68, p71-72, p77-78, p83).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed by March 31 of the following year with the mass balance (RR-5, RR-10, RR-12) and any quantified leakage; records kept at least three years; injected volumes and pressures also reported to TRRC under Class II rules (H-10, annual H-5 MIT); flare/blowdown events documented and reported to TRRC and EPA. No commitment to publish or share monitoring data (p78, p80-81, p83, p86).
notes: Many pages are figure-only with no text (e.g., p3, 12, 14, 17, 19, 24, 36, 38, 39, 42, 48-51, 53, 56, 60, 61, 63, 69, 70, 73, 74, 76); Appendices A-C (cross section, safety plot plan with detector locations, well lists) are referenced but not in the extracted text, so detector counts and locations cannot be verified. The well has injected acid gas since April 2012; the statement that injection 'begins' in Q3 2025 (p81) refers to the start of Subpart RR reporting. Section 6.3 says pressures recorded before injection under the plan 'could include' wellhead, annular and bottomhole pressures 'for example', so the operational pressure baseline is tentatively worded and coded 'unclear'. Annulus pressure frequency is coded continuous because the plan discusses annular pressure changes within the SCADA continuous-monitoring paragraph (p71), though the annulus gauge is not explicitly said to be SCADA-connected. Table 13 lists 'Seismic monitoring station - Continuous', but the text shows this is the public TexNet station 40 km away; the operator's own commitment is to review catalogs with no stated frequency. The atmospheric H2S/CO2 baseline (p68) is a one-time measurement with no ongoing atmospheric program, so atmospheric_co2 is coded mentioned_only. The two observation wells are completed in the Woodbine injection zone, so there is no above-zone monitoring. No production occurs from the Woodbine (p80). Minor inconsistencies: MASIP is given as 1,800 psig (p2) and 1,850 psig (p47, 52); seismicity review radius stated as 9.08 km in Table 12 but 25 km in Section 4.5. Table 13 gives visual inspections as daily for surface equipment and 'as needed' for existing wells; the daily figure is used.

plan_title: Archer Daniels Midland Company, ADM Decatur Corn Processing, Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan CCS#2
ama_definition: Set equal to the MMA: the Area of Review from the Class VI permit plus a half-mile buffer, held constant through injection and the 10-year post-injection period (p12, p14).
mma_definition: The permit Area of Review plus a half-mile buffer, i.e. the stabilized plume (modeled to stabilize 4 years after injection, 6.5 million t total from CCS#1 and CCS#2) plus a half mile, radius about 8,260 ft (p12, p14).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Only surface components (the ~5,000 ft pipeline and wellhead) are rated 'possible'; injection/monitoring wells are 'highly improbable', faults/fractures and confining-zone limitations 'highly improbable to nearly impossible', and abandoned wells 'almost impossible' because none penetrate the Eau Claire seal (p15-18).
baseline_summary: Pre-injection baselines: groundwater quality/geochemistry (completed 08/09/2015, accepted range set statistically with ProUCL at 95% limits), injection-well pulsed neutron and temperature logs (9/30/2015) and shut-in DTS profile (12/31/2016), MIT logs and pressure tests on CCS#2 and VW#2 (2012-2015), RST logs in CCS#1, CCS#2, VW#1, VW#2 (2014-2016), 3D seismic and VSP surveys (2011, 2015), and pre-injection seismicity. Injection and annulus pressures are explicitly not baseline parameters (p20, p29-32).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with mass balance (CO2 injected by Coriolis meter minus surface leakage and equipment/vented emissions, RR-4/6, RR-10, RR-12); records kept per permit Section N in electronic form at Decatur. Through the incorporated Class VI permit, monitoring results go to EPA's UIC program in semiannual reports, with 24-hour reporting of noncompliance, MIT reports within 30 days and 10-year record retention; seismic events above thresholds reported to the UIC Director and ISGS within 24 hours. No commitment to publish monitoring data (p24, p32-34, p55-58, p65-66).
notes: Hand-coded in session (not by the API batch): the API declined to process this plan. The supplied text file is unreadable: the PDF's embedded fonts lack Unicode mappings, so nearly every page extracted as substitution-cipher garbage. To code it, the public PDF was re-downloaded from the plan_url in sources_national.json (SHA-256 matched the recorded hash) and the needed pages were OCR'd with tesseract; quotes come from that OCR and page numbers are PDF pages (same numbering as the text file). The MRV plan itself is only PDF pages 2-38 and relies on Reference 1 (the CCS#2 Class VI permit, p42-282: Attachment C Testing and Monitoring Plan p90-119, QASP p120-223, PISC plan p229-259, emergency plan p260-274) and Reference 2 (2011 permit application, p284-594); rows draw on these incorporated documents. Several QASP tables are rotated (p130-145) and were not read. Wells: the plan covers only CCS#2 (permit IL-115-6A-0001); CCS#1 (the IBDP well, separate permit IL-115-6A-0002) is not an injector under this plan but is used as a monitoring point (downhole P/T, DTS, RST logs). Commitments differ by well: DTS and annual MIT are described for CCS#2; Mt. Simon fluid sampling at VW#2 annually but VW#1 only years 1-3; Ironton-Galesville P/T continuous at VW#2 but VW#1 only years 1-3; VSP used GM#1 near CCS#1; St. Peter monitoring at GM#2; baseline MIT on CCS#2 and VW#2. Inconsistencies: minimum surface annulus pressure is 100 psi in the MRV plan (p29) but 400 psi in Attachment C (p94); the MRV calls the Pennsylvanian bedrock the lowermost USDW (p7) but later the St. Peter (p22); total injection given as 6 million t (p7) and 6.5 million t (p12); repeat 3D seismic is dated year 2 (2019) in Attachment C, est. 2020 in the PISC plan, and 2021 in the MRV plan. The MRV plan cites 'Section 5' for groundwater monitoring, which appears to mean Section 9.1.2.2. Reservoir-pressure baseline coded 'unclear' because the plan lists 'pressure front data' as baseline but names no pre-injection pressure measurement for it. Soil gas and surface air coded mentioned_only (only 'if required by the Director'; the application says neither is proposed).

plan_title: Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan Barnett RDC #1 Wise County, Texas
ama_definition: The AMA is set equal to the MMA (the 50-year post-injection stabilized plume plus a half-mile buffer), which the plan says exceeds the 98.449 superposition of year-14 and year-19 plume areas (p35).
mma_definition: The modeled free-phase CO2 plume (5% molar cutoff) at its stabilized extent 50 years after a 12-year injection period, plus a half-mile buffer; about 4.28 square miles, reaching 1.62 miles from the injector (p34).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Only surface equipment is rated 'possible' (<100 MT per event); well penetrations and surface equipment are named as the only existing pathways, while existing/future wells, faults and fractures, confining layers, seismicity and lateral migration are rated improbable (p34-35, p45).
baseline_summary: Mixed: operational SCADA data used to flag deviations from expected performance; pre-injection baseline groundwater quality from one new groundwater well sampled by a third-party lab; baseline seismicity from historical USGS and TexNet catalogs augmented by dCarbon's own array. Baseline data to be collected before injection begins (p53, p57).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance (Equations RR-5, RR-10, RR-12) and any leakage estimates with methodology; leak quantities and composition variation to be included in recurring regulatory filings; records kept at least three years. Leaks managed per Texas regulations and TRRC permit conditions, but no explicit commitment to publish measurement data or report monitoring results to the state (p37, p47, p49-50, p54-56, p59).
notes: Figure pages are largely images but monitoring sections are complete in text; Attachments A and B (permits, legacy well records) are referenced but not included. Monitoring period is 12 years of injection plus two post-injection years (p35, p46). Frequencies for annulus pressure and the seismic array are coded 'continuous' because they are permanent downhole gauges/arrays described alongside continuous automated monitoring, but the plan does not state a frequency for them explicitly. Reservoir_pressure baseline marked 'unclear': a pressure fall-off test during construction will check model assumptions and later periodic PFOTs look for unexpected increases, but the plan does not call the first test a baseline. Atmospheric methods (UAV CO2 sensor, eddy covariance, open-path lasers, fixed CO2 systems from an environmental services vendor) are described at length as possible quantification tools using 'could' and 'will consider' language, so coded mentioned_only rather than conditional. FLIR leak surveys are folded into fixed_gas_detectors per the coding convention; their frequency is 'recurring' with no number. Groundwater: the plan commits to one new 'deep' groundwater monitoring well near the injection site, not a network; shallow TDS data will also be collected once during drilling (p20). Production_monitoring is not_found because this is a disposal well with no production (p54). Cement bond logs are a construction QA step, coded mentioned_only.

plan_title: Blue Flint Sequester Company, LLC Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan
ama_definition: The North Dakota area of review (AOR), a 1-mile buffer around the projected stabilized CO2 plume rounded to the nearest 40-acre tract, serves as the AMA until facility closure, with monitoring from about one year pre-injection through 20 years of injection and at least 10 years post-injection (p12-14).
mma_definition: The MMA is the same AOR boundary (stabilized plume plus 1-mile buffer, rounded to 40-acre tracts), which exceeds the half-mile Subpart RR minimum (p12-14).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Every pathway is rated very low. The injection well (MAG 1), the monitoring well (MAG 2) and surface equipment (flowline, wellhead) are the only pathways given active mitigation and monitoring; the Class I disposal well, two plugged exploration wells, the suspected Stanton Fault, seismicity, lateral migration, seal diffusivity and future drilling are judged not realistic pathways (p14-19, p21-25).
baseline_summary: A true pre-injection baseline, started September 2022 and running about one year to capture seasons: ambient air and soil gas (O2, N2, CO2, stable and radiocarbon isotopes) at five locations, groundwater chemistry at up to five existing shallow wells plus a new Fox Hills USDW well next to MAG 1 and historical data from 15 Falkirk Mining wells; baseline casing inspection, temperature and pulsed-neutron logs, annulus pressure tests and a pressure falloff test in the wells; and a baseline 2D seismic survey, possibly a VSP (p26, p28-30).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance (Equations RR-4, RR-10, RR-12), expected to be filed March 31 with other GHG reports; records kept at least three years. Also commits to North Dakota UIC reporting under NDAC 43-05-01-18 (24-hour and 30-day reporting) and to a facility closure application to the state. No commitment to publish measurement data (p28, p32-34).
notes: Cover page carries no version number or date; the plan references a state SFP application of October 2022 and a March 2023 hearing. No image-only pages, but figures (maps, seismic sections) have captions only. Much detail is deferred to the state permit (R1 sections), including the surface leak detection plan, worker safety plan and QASP, so personal monitors and detection thresholds are not described here. Sampling listed as '3-4 seasonal samples' per year is coded as quarterly. Shallow groundwater wells are sampled only for baseline (NA during injection, TBD post-injection); only the Fox Hills USDW well continues during injection. Above-zone monitoring is coded committed although it is done only by pulsed-neutron logs in MAG 2, which overlaps the cased_hole_logging row. MAG 2's completion interval is not stated. VSP is a feasibility evaluation only ('may'). Saline storage with no production, so production_monitoring is not_found. Passive seismic relies on the USGS network with unspecified supplementation.

plan_title: Booker Field Area (BFA) MONITORING, REPORTING AND VERIFICATION PLAN (MRV) CapturePoint LLC
ama_definition: The BFA unit boundary plus a half-mile buffer, which the plan says will contain the free-phase plume through year t+5 (p26-27).
mma_definition: Same as the AMA: the BFA boundary plus a half-mile buffer (p7, p27).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: The plan treats wellbores (especially poorly cemented legacy wells) and surface equipment as the realistic pathways; faults/fractures, seal leakage, lateral migration and seismicity are all rated unlikely, with surface equipment leaks of 0.1-2 MT/yr and well or seal leaks of 5-20 MT once per 50 years given as magnitudes (p27-35, p37).
baseline_summary: No operator pre-injection environmental baseline. Baseline is ongoing operational data (injection well pressures and rates, pattern surveillance). NOAA Moody, Texas atmospheric CO2 data would serve as background for any soil-flux measurement, and a TWDB database pre-injection water analysis (State Well 04-36-201) is the reference for any Ogallala water sample (p37-38).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance; any leak quantification method would be described in that report. Leaks also reported to the TRRC under Rule 20 with estimated quantities, and MIT results filed on TRRC Form H-5. Records retained per 98.3(g). No commitment to publish measurement data (p36-38, p43-44).
notes: Pages 1-4 are cover and table of contents; figure pages (e.g., 19, 21, 25, 29, 31, 35) carry little text but no monitoring section appears to be lost to image-only pages. Inspection frequency is inconsistent: Section 5.4 says daily visual inspection of surface equipment, Table 1 says weekly field inspection (coded daily, both cited). Reservoir pressure is named only as an example on p35 and Table 1 relies on WAG skid pressure and pressures encountered when new wells are drilled for faults, seals, lateral migration and seismicity, so no dedicated reservoir, above-zone, soil, groundwater or seismic monitoring is committed. Groundwater coded mentioned_only because the plan explicitly says no routine sampling and does not commit to sample on a trigger, though it references a TWDB pre-injection analysis as a comparison value. Production test frequency is 30-60 days, coded monthly. The plan is dated November 2023 but states implementation begins April 1, 2023 when the Arkalon capture upgrade is operational, and elsewhere describes the MRV period as July 2023-August 2035. Injected mass for the mass balance comes from the purchase and recycle totalizer meters, not per-well turbine meters. Three former GHGRP facility IDs (544680, 544681, 544682) were merged into 544681.

plan_title: Camrick Field Area (CFA) MONITORING, REPORTING AND VERIFICATION PLAN (MRV) CapturePoint LLC
ama_definition: The Camrick Field Area unitized leases plus an all-around half-mile buffer, which the plan says it monitors in its entirety; the figure captions, however, show the AMA excluding a red hashed rectangle that the MMA includes (p21-23).
mma_definition: The boundary of the Camrick Field Area plus a half-mile buffer, sized to hold up to 140 Bscf of injected CO2 and all areas of the CFA that could be used for future injection (p6, p20-22).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Every pathway is rated unlikely; poorly completed or cemented legacy wellbores are named the most likely pathway, with surface equipment leaks handled through Subpart W. Faults, fractures, lateral migration, seal failure and seismicity are dismissed largely on the basis of Farnsworth Unit analog studies (p23-30, p32).
baseline_summary: No CFA-specific pre-injection environmental baseline. Section 5 offers NOAA Moody, Texas atmospheric CO2 data (and a defunct Farnsworth eddy tower) as background values for soil CO2, says groundwater is not routinely sampled, and otherwise relies on daily visual inspection and UIC well surveillance (p32-33).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance, Subpart W surface-equipment estimates and the methodology used for any event-driven leak quantification (p31, p35-37); leaks also reported to OCC/TRRC with measured or estimated quantities under their fire/break/leak rules (p33). Records kept per 98.3(g) and 98.447 (p39). No commitment to publish measurement data.
notes: Text defines both AMA and MMA as the CFA plus a half-mile buffer, but the Figure 3.1-1/3.1-2 captions say the AMA excludes a red hashed rectangle that the MMA includes (p21-22). Inspection frequency is inconsistent: Section 5.4 says surface equipment is inspected daily, while Table 1 says weekly field inspection (p31-32); coded as daily with the discrepancy noted. Table 1 is the only place injection pressure monitoring ('pressure in WAG skids') is described; no SCADA or alarm set points are given. Reservoir pressure appears only as an example in the seismicity paragraph, so coded mentioned_only. MIT interval is not stated. Section 4 cross-references to 'Sections 4.5 and 4.6' for detection and quantification appear to be stale pointers to Sections 4.7 and 4.8. Section 5 ('baselines') describes Farnsworth Unit and NOAA data rather than any CFA measurement; no soil gas, groundwater or atmospheric program is committed at the CFA. Production well test interval of 30-60 days was coded as monthly. Most figure pages (p7, 16, 24-27) are images with captions only; no text appears lost.

plan_title: Riverside Energy Michigan, LLC Chester 21-29N-02W Storage Facility Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan
ama_definition: The Chester 21-29N-02W Reef Structure area (regularized to the nearest 10-acre square) plus a half-mile buffer in all directions, set for a 10-year period covering the expected project life; the plume is projected to stay inside the reef (p23-25).
mma_definition: Identical to the AMA: the reef structure plus a half-mile buffer, since the stabilized plume is expected to remain within the compartmentalized reef (p25).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: No pathway is rated more than low. Surface equipment between the meter and wellhead and the single injection wellbore are treated as the realistic ones and receive the most monitoring; legacy wells and future wells are low; faults, seismicity, confining layers and lateral migration are very low (p26-32).
baseline_summary: Pre-injection baselines are collected: MIT and annular pressure test, initial annular fluid volume, tubing and annulus wellhead pressures, initial bottomhole pressure and temperature gradient survey, one groundwater sample from the pad water well, and a baseline OGI survey of surface equipment; target injection rates from analog reefs and the model serve as operating baselines (p34-36).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with mass balance (RR-4, RR-10, RR-12) and quarterly averages of flow rate and mass injected; records kept per 98.3(g) and three years per 98.447. Well records and injection data will be shared with Michigan-EGLE; no commitment to publish monitoring data (p29, p36-41).
notes: Reservoir pressure and temperature surveys are run in the injection well itself (no observation well); coded as semiannual because the first two years are every six months before dropping to annual. Groundwater well depth is given as approx. 100 ft in Section 6.4 (p35) but 60 ft in Table 4 (p28); one of two Riverside water wells on the pad is retained for monitoring. The State Chester 2-22 Dundee brine disposal well is monitored and MIT-tested by a different operator and is not part of this plan's monitoring. Table 2 lists the injection well as 'Permit pending' while Section 1.4 says the permit was issued 1/10/2025. Passive seismic frequency coded event_driven because it is a notification subscription. Figures are captioned images with no additional text; no sections appear missing.

plan_title: Core CO2 Services Niagaran Reef CO2 Sequestration Project CO2 Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan
uic_class_per_plan: II-D (initial wells; Class VI permit applications being prepared for future wells)
ama_definition: The 30 pinnacle reefs listed in Appendix A-1 (initially Charlton 10 and Chester 12 active, the rest idle), each defined by its seismic/well-control reef boundary plus a one-half mile buffer, for a 20-year injection period (p33-36).
mma_definition: The whole band of hydrocarbon-bearing Niagaran pinnacle reefs of the NNPRT across northern lower Michigan from Presque Isle County to Manistee County, plus a half-mile buffer north and south of the reef trend (p30-31).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Pipeline and surface equipment is the only pathway rated above low (medium likelihood, low magnitude). Wellbores penetrating the reef are called the most likely subsurface pathway but rated low because of well construction, cement evaluation and MIT. Faults, seismicity, lateral migration out of a reef, and diffuse seal leakage are all rated low (p37-39, p41-44).
baseline_summary: Mainly operational data: daily field inspections, SCADA injection rate/pressure against target values, annular pressure and MIT results, and quarterly handheld CO2 readings compared for 'statistically significant' deviations (p51-52). The plan also requires 'baseline monitoring' for at least one month (30 days) before injection at each reef moving from Pending to Active, but does not say which measurements that baseline includes (p29, p34, p46, p55).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report through e-GGRT with the mass balance (RR-1/RR-4/RR-6/RR-10/RR-12) and any quantified leakage events; the annual report also carries changes to reef/well inventory, maps of reefs entering Pending/Active status, an affirmative statement that no new leakage pathways exist, and an attestation when a reef is qualified (p9, p27-29, p33-34, p52-55). MIT and workover results go to EGLE/EPA; data is also used for EGLE reporting (p26, p47). A stabilization report is planned 2-3 years after injection ends at a reef (p36, p50-51). Records kept at least 3 years. Idle reef locations are proprietary; no commitment to publish measurement data.
notes: Purpose coded co2_disposal: the initial four wells are to be permitted by EGLE as Class II-D for 'disposal of oilfield waste' (Table A-1 labels them 'Class IID-AGI'), with two Class VI applications being prepared for EPA Region V; no hydrocarbons are produced, so production_monitoring is genuinely absent rather than omitted (p9, p22, p45). Pages 20, 22, 32 and 42 are figure-only pages; no monitoring text appears lost. Section 5.5.1 says 'continual pressure monitoring in the injection zone' (p47), which in context appears to mean SCADA wellhead pressure; the only explicit reservoir pressure measurement is the 'episodic surveys' on p49 with no stated interval, so reservoir_pressure is coded periodic_unspecified. Pre-injection qualification requires a stabilized reservoir pressure below 20% of discovery pressure (p34), which could be read as a baseline, hence 'unclear'. The plan requires 'baseline monitoring' for at least one month / 30 days before injection at each new reef (p34, p46, p55) but never lists what that baseline comprises; the handheld CO2 and material-balance rows are therefore marked baseline 'unclear'. Quarterly handheld CO2 readings at well locations are coded as atmospheric_co2 (the plan calls it 'surface CO2 monitoring' with hand-held units; no soil probes or flux chambers are mentioned). The 'fixed CO2 monitors throughout the gas plant facility' appear only in Table 2 (p47) with no description of the gas plant. Monitoring is phased by reef status (Idle: none; Pending: baseline; Active: SCADA plus handheld CO2; Passive post-injection: handheld CO2 only until release; Plugged-Released: none) (p46). Idle reef locations are withheld as proprietary; reef additions beyond the 30 listed require a revised plan, while well/reef/equipment changes within the list are handled through the annual report (p27-29, p34). Equation RR-12 is described as 'incidentally stored' (p54), a leftover from the EOR template.

plan_title: Core Energy Northern Niagaran Pinnacle Reef Trend (NNPRT) CO2 Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The AMA is the Unit Area boundary of each individual reef/field as set in the MDEQ Supervisor of Wells order authorizing that EOR project, because each reef is a sealed compartment (p27-28).
mma_definition: The MMA is the whole band of hydrocarbon-bearing Niagaran pinnacle reefs along the northern Michigan Basin from Lake Huron to Lake Michigan, plus a half-mile buffer around the reefs (p28-29).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Existing wellbores are called the most likely pathway but rated very small risk given well construction and integrity studies; pipelines and surface equipment are treated as a potential risk handled by inspection and Subpart W. Faults, seismicity, lateral migration out of a reef, and diffuse seal leakage are all rated highly unlikely (p31-36).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline. The baseline is daily operational data (injection rates/pressures against targets, production forecasts, casing pressure, fill-up tests, MITs) and daily visual rounds, used to flag variances (p41-42). Well pressure survey histories built over time serve the same role for bottom-hole pressure (p39). A separate 'baseline accounting' of 2.11 Mt CO2 injected since 1996 is an inventory figure, not a monitoring baseline (p20).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance and any event-driven leak quantification, reconciled with an internal Subpart W report; facility and well changes are to be reported in the annual report rather than by plan revision; MIT and workover results go to EPA UIC before injection resumes; a closure report is promised for any abandoned reef; leak-event records kept at least three years. No commitment to publish measurement data (p26-27, p38-42, p46-48).
notes: Pages 22 (Figure 13 process flow diagram), 49 and 58 (pipeline map) are image-only; meter numbering is described in text only. The plan says wells are monitored 'through continual pressure monitoring in the injection zone (as described in Section 5.1)' (p40), but Section 5.1 describes only flow, pressure and composition data in the HMI, while Section 5.5.1 describes reservoir pressure as episodic 3-7 day surveys; reservoir_pressure frequency is therefore recorded as periodic_unspecified. Seismicity is discussed only as a hazard assessment (p35); no seismic network monitoring is mentioned, so passive_seismic is not_found. Appendix I lists several 'OBS' observation wells (Bagley, Chester 16) but the plan does not describe any monitoring program at them beyond production/pressure surveillance. Section 7.4 cites Sections 5.1.5-5.1.7, which do not exist. Unusual accounting: recycled Dover 36 gas is counted as CO2 'received' under RR-1 until the 2.11 Mt pre-2018 inventory is reached (p43); the mass balance starts at zero as of January 1, 2018 (p20, p47). Facility changes (new reefs, wells, sources, pipelines) are to be handled through the annual report rather than MRV plan revisions (p26-27).

plan_title: Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan Cotton Cove CCS 1
ama_definition: The AMA is set equal to the MMA because the MMA (94-year post-injection plume plus half-mile buffer) already exceeds the 40 CFR 98.449 definition for a 12-year injection period (p35).
mma_definition: The modeled free-phase CO2 plume after it stabilizes 94 years post-injection (5% gas saturation cutoff) plus an all-around half-mile buffer, about 3.07 square miles reaching 1.5 miles from the injector (p34).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Surface equipment is the only pathway rated 'possible'; existing wells are 'unlikely' (via faults into the Barnett Shale and then produced gas); not-yet-drilled wells, faults/fractures, confining layers, seismicity and lateral migration are 'improbable'. The plan states that well penetrations and surface equipment are the only real pathways (p35, p37-38).
baseline_summary: Three pre-injection baselines: groundwater quality from one or more groundwater wells near the site (plus baseline sampling of available water wells in the MMA), gas composition including CO2 from the Barnett Shale producers acting as above-zone monitoring wells, and seismicity from USGS/TexNet records (TexNet since 2017) and the operator's own array since 2023. Baseline data collection starts in 2025, injection in 2026 (p49-51, p53).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR monitoring report with mass balance (Eq. RR-12) and any leakage estimates and methods; flow and composition data compiled quarterly; records kept at least five years. Abnormal pressure or seismicity concerns are reported to the TRRC per permit conditions. MRV plan to be modified to Eq. RR-11 if CO2 reaches the Barnett wells. No commitment to publish measurement data (p44, p47, p49, p52-55).
notes: Attachment A (W-14/W-1 permits, p57) contains only a title in the extracted text. Sections are misnumbered in the plan (3.1 appears before section 3). production_monitoring is coded not_found because this is a disposal well with no production; the sampling of third-party Barnett Shale producers is coded under above_zone_monitoring, and the plan says dCarbon will 'endeavor to work with' those operators, so access is not fully in its control; no routine sampling frequency is given (quarterly sampling is only promised after a leak is found). Fixed CO2/O2 detectors are stated as a facility design feature (p35) and as alarm sources (p46, p52) but the QA section hedges with 'gas detectors, if employed' (p54); coded committed with this caveat. Personal gas monitors are described as detecting H2S and O2, not necessarily CO2, and the stream contains no H2S. The reservoir_pressure row combines an annual bottomhole P/T measurement with PFOTs of unstated frequency. Atmospheric and other quantification technologies (UAV, eddy covariance, open-path lasers, NDIR, soil flux) are all 'could'/'will consider' language and coded mentioned_only rather than conditional.

plan_title: Elk Hills A1-A2 and 26R CO2 Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan
ama_definition: The modeled plume area at t = three years after injection ends (30 years after start) plus a half-mile buffer; one AMA held for 30 years and treated as functionally equivalent to the MMA (p18, p21).
mma_definition: The modeled extent of the CO2 plume at 100 years post-injection plus a half-mile buffer, shown as the blue line in Figure 8 (p18, p20).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Only existing wellbores and pipelines/surface equipment are treated as realistic (low likelihood; wellbore leakage magnitude bounded at under 1% of injection). Faults, seismicity, previous operations, lateral migration, future drilling and diffuse seal leakage are rated negligible or not anticipated (p24-31).
baseline_summary: Pre-injection baselines: fluid chemistry and pressure/temperature at each monitoring well collected during construction (quarterly sampling and continuous P/T at above-confining-zone wells; one-time chemistry plus continuous P/T in the injection zone), and at least 12 months of seismic network data before first injection. Operational data (injection set-points, inspections, personal monitor alarms) also serve as a working baseline for flagging excursions (p38-40).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report (filed March 31 with other GHG reports) with mass balance and estimated leakage; records kept at least three years. Table 4 notes parallel reporting of well incidents to CalGEM or EPA UIC and of surface leaks under Subpart W; monitoring well procedures follow the Class VI permit. No commitment to publish measurement data (p32, p39-40, p43-44).
notes: Figure and equation pages (7-12, 14, 16, 19, 20, 22, 23, 27, 29, 31, 35 and the equations in Section 7) are largely image-only. production_monitoring is not_found because the plan states no CO2 will be produced or recycled (p34); Table 4 does list 'anomalous pressure or gas composition from productive shallower zones' as a detector for abandoned-well leakage, presumably from existing Etchegoin production, but no program is described (p32). MIT frequency conflicts: Table 5 says annual (p34) while Section 4.2 says before injection, after workovers or per UIC schedule (p24-25); annual used. Above-zone and groundwater quarterly sampling frequencies come from Appendix 11.6 tables for the injection phase; Section 6.3 describes the same quarterly/continuous scheme for the baseline period. Well list names plume well 374-36R but the monitoring table names 376-36R (p51-52). Geophysical plume monitoring (p31) is a bare commitment deferred to the Class VI permit, so it is coded under other rather than active_seismic. The seismic network's 'near real-time' telemetry and Mw 0.0 detection threshold are design specifications; response actions are deferred to the Class VI permit except the Mw 2.0 damage trigger (p38). Plan implementation anticipated Q1 2025 or 90 days after EPA approval (p43).

plan_title: Blue Spruce Operating LLC Dry Piney "Jackalope" Gas Processing Facility & Dry Piney State Acid Gas Injection Wells Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting and Verification Plan
plan_version_or_date: Original Submission - August 2025; First Revision - October 2025; Second Revision - December 2025 (2nd revision submittal December 11, 2025)
ama_definition: BSO sets the AMA equal to the MMA by choosing t = 2128 (end of a 50-year injection period plus 50-year stabilization), so the plume-plus-buffer area including the fault pathways coincides with the MMA polygon (p48-49).
mma_definition: The union of the modeled 50-year (2078) and stabilized 100-year (2128) free-phase plume outlines (defined as >0.5% net incremental CO2 saturation above in-situ CO2) plus a half-mile buffer, further extended by a half-mile buffer around faults that extend beyond the stabilized plume (p44-48).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Every pathway is rated 'very low' overall risk. Surface equipment (AGI pipeline, flanges, wellheads) is described as the most likely leak source but 'very unlikely' because of H2S detection and design (p50-52). The plugged Tip Top T62X-16S, the only non-BSO well penetrating the injection zone, is rated 'unlikely' (p54-59). Faults 5, 6 and 7, which extend through the Triassic Evaporite seal into the Frontier, are rated 'unlikely' likelihood but insignificant magnitude; all other faults, confining units, lateral migration and seismicity are 'very unlikely' (p58-73).
baseline_summary: A pre-injection environmental baseline program starting in 2027, at least 12 months before the expected October 2028 start of injection (p92): quarterly produced-gas composition (including CO2, H2S and helium) from a subset of third-party shallow gas wells for 12 months (p85-86); monthly groundwater chemistry from existing water wells for 12 months (p87-88); monthly soil CO2 flux at plugged wells and above faults for 12 months (p88-89); a seismic baseline from historical ANSS data (p86-87); and, if adopted, semiannual satellite/Lidar imaging for two years (p85). Operational baseline is 0 ppm H2S with no alarms (p84) and DCS set points (p85).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report using Equation RR-12 (injected minus surface leakage minus equipment leaks), with CO2 received set equal to CO2 injected (p89-92); records kept at least three years (p94). BSO says it will assume responsibility for 'monitoring, recording, and reporting' data from the CO2 monitoring network and that the seismic station can 'report data to third parties as necessary' and will generate periodic seismic reports (p85-86); produced-gas and groundwater reports will be developed internally (p86-87). A revised MRV plan would be submitted if the plume exceeds the modeled area (p80). No commitment to publish measurement data; WOGCC Class II testing/monitoring conditions are referenced but no state reporting commitment is spelled out (p85).
notes: Plan is pre-injection (first injection expected October 2028); all commitments are future tense. Figures are image-only (e.g., p10, 12, 14-17, 24-25, 29-33, 35-40, 43-48, 50, 53-54, 56, 62, 65-66, 68, 72); Appendix B wellbore diagram (p119) has no text; Appendix D (p122-130) is OCR of scanned lab reports; bold/italic marking of baseline candidate wells in Appendices A and C is lost in extraction. Coding choices: (1) third-party shallow gas well composition sampling is coded under above_zone_monitoring because the Frontier/Bear River wells sit above the Triassic Evaporite confining zone; it is not EOR production monitoring, so production_monitoring is not_found. It is hedged 'to the extent possible' and depends on other operators, so a reader could reasonably downgrade it to conditional. (2) Satellite hyperspectral/Lidar imaging appears in Table 5.1 and has a stated schedule in 6.3 (semiannual two years, then annual), but every narrative mention says BSO is 'investigating' its use and 'would' employ it, so it is coded mentioned_only; this is the weakest supportable level, and it could be read as committed. (3) DTS/DAS fiber is coded as other rather than cased_hole_logging since it is a permanent sensor, not a logging run. (4) In-well gauges and DTS/DAS are described only for the Dry Piney State 12-16 (Section 5.3.1), though Table 5.1 lists in-well pressure/temperature sensors for all AGI wells. (5) Soil flux frequency is quarterly for three years post-baseline then annual; groundwater is quarterly post-baseline; shallow-well gas is annual post-baseline. Inconsistencies: personal H2S alarm stated as 5 ppm (p51) and 10 ppm (p85); text repeatedly cites a 'Section 6.9' that does not exist; Figure 2.6 and Appendix E are cited for gas analyses that are actually Table 2.6 and Appendix D. Plan states monitoring continues through injection and the 50-year post-injection period (p74). Plan itself notes it would assume 1-3 months (up to ~1.25 Mt) to detect leakage via shallow wells and 12-18 months (4.5-6.75 Mt) via surface methods (p78-82). Permanent DTS/DAS fiber is coded under cased_hole_logging, as in v1.3.

plan_title: Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan for the Eastern Wyoming Sequestration Hub, Laramie County, Wyoming
ama_definition: The modeled free-phase CO2 plume area 50 years after injection ends plus a 0.5-mile buffer (Area #1), which is functionally the same as the MMA; one AMA for the whole project life (p31).
mma_definition: The stabilized CO2 plume extent (2 percent saturation cutoff, 50 years after end of injection) plus a 0.5-mile all-around buffer, shown on Figure 10 (p31-32).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Pipelines/surface equipment (wear at flanges, relief valves, accidents) and wellbores (injection wells, M-1 wells, three abandoned penetrations, one of which, Fritz 1, needs remedial plugging) are rated 'minor' likelihood; confining zone, seismicity, lateral migration and future drilling are rated negligible or not anticipated (p33-37).
baseline_summary: A mixed baseline: one year of pre-injection groundwater, soil gas and atmospheric sampling around each injection well, semiannual pre-injection USDW/M-1 fluid sampling and continuous M-1 pressure/temperature, existing 2D/3D seismic as the plume baseline, and historical USGS seismicity; operating parameters are also continuously monitored against set points (p39, p43-45, p54).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the RR-12 mass balance, surface leakage and vented/fugitive emissions under 98.446(f)(3); new wells or status changes noted in the annual report; inspection and test records kept available for EPA review. Class VI monitoring follows WDEQ Chapter 24 permits. No commitment to publish measurement data (p7, p33, p42-43, p47-48, p50-51).
notes: Pages 9, 12, 13, 16-21, 26-30, 32, 38 and 39 are figure pages with no extracted text; Figure 10 (p32), which shows monitoring well, eddy covariance tower and soil gas locations, is image-only, so locations are known only from the text and Appendices A-B. Production_monitoring is recorded not_found because the plan states no CO2 is produced, entrained or recycled (p40). Reservoir_pressure is coded mentioned_only: the plan mentions 'downhole pressure and temperature measurements' for plume stabilization (p44) but never identifies injection-zone gauges; the M-1 gauges monitor the Sundance above the confining zone. DTS/DAS fiber behind casing in M-1 wells is described as installed or planned 'for future utility' (p34), i.e. not an active commitment beyond the annual DTS/temperature logs. 'Biannual' surface safety valve testing (p42) is ambiguous (twice yearly vs every two years); frequency row coded annual on the master valve test. The plan says six M-1 wells but only Juniper M-1 and Spirea M-1R fully penetrate the confining zone (p15). Point-source monitoring 'once per year at other locations' (p41) does not specify whether abandoned wells (Fritz 1, UPRR Palm 1-21, Cypress M-2) are included. MIT frequency is deferred to WDEQ Class VI permits. The Class VI permits are cited as governing the 2D seismic and groundwater protocols but are not reproduced.

plan_title: Farnsworth Unit, Texas (FWU) MONITORING, REPORTING, AND VERIFICATION PLAN
ama_definition: The entire Farnsworth Unit, because activity is expected to expand from the western half to the eastern half on an uncertain schedule (p24).
mma_definition: The Farnsworth Unit boundary plus a one-half mile buffer, justified by simulation showing the free-phase plume stays within the modeled area through five years after injection ends (p6, p21-23).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Wellbores (especially poorly completed or cemented legacy wells) and surface equipment are treated as the realistic pathways; faults/fractures, lateral migration, seal failure and seismicity are all rated unlikely (p24-35).
baseline_summary: The plan calls its baseline the combination of ongoing operational monitoring plus Southwest Partnership (SWP) research data collected since 2013: Ogallala groundwater sampling at 14 wells, soil CO2 flux of 3-15 umol/m2/s at 94 collars, and an atmospheric CO2 baseline of 390±10 ppmv from an eddy tower; daily equipment inspection and well surveillance are also cited (p35-39).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance; any leak quantification method is reported in that submission and reconciled against the Subpart W report (p34-35). Leaks are also reported to TRRC under Rule 20 with measured or estimated quantities (p40). Records retained per 98.3(g)/98.447 (p46-47). No commitment to publish measurement data.
notes: Much of the environmental monitoring described (groundwater, soil flux, eddy tower, downhole gauges, DTS, geophones, seismometers) was done by the Southwest Regional Partnership as research; the plan uses it to establish baselines but says the #13-10 instrumentation will not be an ongoing part of the MRV plan and that Perdure is unlikely to continue groundwater sampling, with no stated commitment on soil flux or atmospheric monitoring, so these are coded mentioned_only. Inspection frequency is inconsistent: Section 5.4 says daily surface equipment inspection while Table 1 says weekly field inspection. No SCADA system is described; pressure monitoring is 'continuous monitoring of pressure in WAG skids'. MIT interval is not stated. The plan's internal cross-references to 'Sections 4.5 and 4.6' for detection/quantification actually point to Sections 4.7 and 4.8. Implementation is tied to the new capture facility starting January 1, 2022 (p43). Pages 22, 23, 30, 31 and 39 are mostly figures; the text of Table 1 is on p34.

plan_title: Great Plains CO2 Sequestration Project Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan, Class VI Well, Reporting Number: 523812
ama_definition: The North Dakota AOR, i.e. the storage facility area (modeled plume extent plus a 1-mile buffer rounded to 40-acre tracts), which the plan says exceeds the Subpart RR AMA and so serves as the AMA (p12-13).
mma_definition: The same AOR also serves as the MMA, since it exceeds the Subpart RR MMA calculated with t at injection cessation (p13-14).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Every pathway is rated unlikely. Wellbores (two Class I disposal wells ANG #1 and #2, the plugged Herrmann 1, and the six Coteau injectors) and surface components (pipeline, flowlines, wellheads) get the most attention and are the focus of the monitoring; faults, seismicity, lateral migration, seal diffusivity and future drilling are rated very unlikely (p15-21).
baseline_summary: Pre-injection baseline monitoring over four seasons: completed soil gas sampling at 11 stations and groundwater sampling at two existing wells (chemistry plus stable and radiocarbon isotopes), planned baseline samples from five new Fox Hills monitoring wells, historical data from 19 CPC shallow wells, and subsurface baselines in each injection well (USIT, pulsed-neutron and temperature logs, bottomhole pressure, annulus pressure tests, falloff tests) plus baseline 2D radial seismic and VSP (p14-15, p23, p26-27).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance (Eq. RR-12), filed with other GHG reports by March 31; records kept at least 3 years in an electronic database. Leak events communicated to the state UIC program director within 24 hours if warranted and injection resumes only with written authorization; a formal AOR reevaluation is submitted every 5 years. No commitment to publish measurement data (p25, p26, p29, p30).
notes: No version or date is printed; implementation is set for September 2022 and references were accessed June 2022. Figures on pp7, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14 are images with no text. Table 4-1 (p23) extracted with interleaved cells; frequencies were reconstructed carefully, but the USIT/PMIT line reads both 'not more frequently than once every 5 years' and 'not less than once every 5 years', so the exact interval is ambiguous. Soil gas and groundwater 'three to four seasonal samples each year' coded as quarterly. The plan leans heavily on the state SFP (Reference 1, Sections 5-7, Appendices A-C) for instrument details, thresholds and QA, which are not included in the text. Reservoir pressure: the quarterly logging schedule is tabulated, while p21 says real-time Broom Creek bottomhole pressure data will be available without naming gauges. Seismicity is discussed only as historical characterization (USGS catalog); no seismic monitoring or network reliance is stated, so passive_seismic is not_found. Saline storage with no production, so production_monitoring is not_found. Personal monitors are not mentioned (worker safety plan referenced only by title).

plan_title: Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan Lima Tango CCS 1
ama_definition: The AMA calculated under 40 CFR 98.449 for a 12-year injection period (t = 12) was smaller than the MMA, so the operator adopts the MMA as the AMA and refers to the combined area as AMA/MMA (p36-37).
mma_definition: The modeled free-phase CO2 plume at stabilization (98 years post-injection, 5% gas-saturation cutoff) plus a half-mile buffer, about 0.88 square miles, with the farthest extent 0.72 miles from the injector (p35).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Only surface equipment leakage is rated 'possible' (<100 MT per event). Existing wells, undrilled permitted wells, faults/fractures, confining layers, seismicity, and lateral migration are all rated 'improbable' because no wells in the AMA/MMA penetrate below about 2,500 ft, mapped faults lie outside the plume, and confining shales are thick (p39-43).
baseline_summary: Three parts: (1) pre-injection groundwater quality from a monitoring well, but only if a freshwater aquifer is found when logging the injection well (quarterly sampling the first year, then possibly annual); (2) a seismicity baseline from TexNet/USGS historical data starting in 2019; (3) operational performance baselines built from continuous injection pressure, temperature, rate and annulus pressure/temperature data once injection begins in 2026 (p49).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance (Equation RR-12; no CO2 produced). Any leakage estimates and the methods used are to be reported in the annual monitoring report; surface-equipment leaks quantified under Subpart W are 'included in recurring reporting'; MRV plan to be updated if new wells are drilled in the MMA. Records kept at least three years. No commitment to publish or share measurement data or to report monitoring results to the TRRC beyond the permit (p40, p45-47, p51, p55).
notes: Pre-operational plan: the well had not been drilled (drilling planned Q3 2025, injection early 2026). Page 60 (Appendix 13.3, W-1/W-14 permits) has no text; pages 35, 37 and 41 contain garbled figure characters. AVO inspection frequency is stated inconsistently: monthly (p40), daily inspections plus monthly AVO (p44), and 'daily to weekly AVO inspections' (p49); coded as monthly with detail noting the others. The only reservoir-pressure measurement is the bottomhole gauge in the injection well itself; there are no observation wells. Groundwater monitoring is explicitly conditional on finding a freshwater response in open-hole logs of the injector (the plan notes no water wells within two miles), so the groundwater baseline exists only in that case. Open-hole logs over each casing interval during drilling (p47) are site characterization, not cased-hole monitoring, so cased_hole_logging is not_found. Section 6.7 lists many quantification technologies (atmospheric sensing, UAV, eddy covariance, open-path lasers, NDIR, soil flux, reservoir models) only as options to be 'considered' if a leak is detected; these are coded mentioned_only. The static/dynamic model is to be updated with core and log data after drilling (p28). Monitoring period stated as the 12-year injection period plus a proposed two-year post-injection period (p44). Risk ranking uses the CARB CCS Protocol likelihood matrix (p38-39).

plan_title: Lisbon Valley, Utah Gas Processing Plant Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan
ama_definition: The half-mile buffer around the modeled free-phase CO2 plume at year 2060 (30 years of injection plus 10 years post-injection), drawn so it also contains the plume projected for 2065 (p37-38).
mma_definition: The combined P10/P50/P90 modeled plume footprint at year 2205 (150 years post-injection, when the plume stabilizes against the graben fault) plus a half-mile buffer; monitoring is proposed to end in 2205 (p35-36, p38).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: None is treated as likely. Surface equipment (flanges and valves on the acid-gas pipeline and plant) is the only pathway given more than negligible likelihood, and even that is rated low (p39). Legacy wells, faults and seal leakage were modeled with NRAP-Open-IAM as zero risk; future drilling, lateral migration and induced seismicity are called negligible or highly unlikely (p39-53).
baseline_summary: A mix: DCS target ranges and trigger thresholds for injection rate, pressure and composition (operational baseline); plus described pre-injection baselines for a suite of MITs on the injector, ambient H2S checks, documented baseline inspections, at least four seasonal rounds of soil CO2 flux at an array of collars (thresholds set at a high percentile), and temperature/pressure/fluid composition at one selected USDW water well (p56-57). Note that injection has been ongoing since 2015, so 'prior to injection' baselines can only be pre-plan or pre-rate-increase.
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report using equations RR-1 to RR-12 (received, injected, surface leakage, sequestered), with surface equipment leaks estimated per Subpart W; quarterly records of received and injected CO2 and annual records of leakage calculations retained under 40 CFR 98.3(g) (p57-64). Annual MIT on the injector under 40 CFR 146.8 (p54). No commitment to publish or share measurement data; no explicit commitment to report monitoring results to the state UIC program, though the plan relies on DOGM/EPA oversight of drilling (p40).
notes: No version number or date is printed; the plan says it takes effect in Q2/Q3 2025 after EPA approval (p62). Prepared by the University of Utah EGI/CSI for GNG Energy. Injection has been ongoing since 2015 (June 1 on p28, July 1 on p62), so section 6 baselines described as 'prior to injection' (MIT suite, inspections, soil flux, USDW well) are ambiguous in timing; coded baseline=yes because the plan describes them as pre-monitoring reference measurements. Personal H2S alarm threshold is given as 10 ppm on p39 and ~5 ppm on p54. Soil flux duration is ambiguous: p55 says seasonal monitoring 'for 5 years following the injection period' while p56-57 refers to flux values collected during and after injection; 5 years post-injection is far shorter than the 150-year monitoring timeframe (p38, p62). reservoir_pressure coded committed on the strength of p46-47 language about pressure and fluid monitoring at the injection well, but this may simply be the DCS wellhead data; no gauges or observation wells are named. The seismic station is only 'suggested' (p53). Section 7.3 states no production, yet section 9.1 contains template text on quarterly sampling of produced gas and a recycle compressor meter, and p48 refers to 'Targa' (apparently copied from another plan). Several figure pages (e.g. p22-24, p26-27, p31-34) are image-only apart from captions; Tables 4 and 5 and the stratigraphic chart on p9 are garbled in extraction but not needed for coding. No annulus pressure, above-zone, logging, deformation or atmospheric CO2 monitoring is described.

plan_title: North Burbank Unit (NBU) CO2 Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The AMA is the North Burbank Unit boundary itself, because injected CO2 is held within the unit by structure and water-curtain injection; it expands as CO2-EOR moves into other parts of the unit (p20-21).
mma_definition: The MMA is the NBU unit boundary plus the required half-mile buffer, since the free-phase plume is expected to stay within the unit (p21).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Only wellbores (about 2,845 wells, roughly 2,394 inactive or abandoned) and pipelines/surface equipment are treated as realistic pathways; faults/fractures, natural and induced seismicity, prior operations, lateral migration, future drilling and diffuse seal leakage are rated improbable or very low (p4, p22-29).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline. The baseline is ongoing operational data: daily field monitoring, SCADA data, target injection rates/pressures, production forecasts, routine inspections, H2S alarms, plant/pipeline set points and MITs, used to flag excursions from expected performance (p34-36).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed with other GHG reports by March 31, containing the mass balance (RR-2 through RR-11, using RCF outlet and satellite/RCF inlet meters rather than per-well meters) and any quantified leakage events; AMA expansions and facility changes are described in the annual report; event records kept at least 3 years. No commitment to publish measurement data or to report monitoring results to the UIC program beyond permit requirements (p21, p34, p36-42).
notes: No image-only pages; figures and the well list (p56-91) carry little monitoring text. Well-test frequency is inconsistent: p23 says each producer is tested about every two months, p31 says once every quarter; quarterly is coded (weaker). MIT is 'periodic (and in many instances an annual)', so coded periodic_unspecified rather than annual. 'Continual, automated pressure monitoring in the injection zone' (p31) cross-references Section 4.1, which describes injection-well pressure, so reservoir_pressure is coded mentioned_only despite several references to reservoir pressure. 'Gas alarms' (p29) appear only in a list with no description. Seismic networks are cited for risk characterization only. Section 7.4 refers to quantification approaches 'in Section 5.1', apparently meaning 5.8. The plan acknowledges a prior operator let small amounts of CO2 move past the western unit boundary (p20, p27-28); response would be quantification and reporting, not added subsurface monitoring. Mass balance uses aggregated RCF/satellite meters because of per-well meter error (p37, p38).

plan_title: Purdy-Bradley Springer Field: Northeast Purdy Springer Unit (NEPSU) / South East Bradley A Unit (SEBAU) Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The combined NEPSU and SEBAU unit boundaries plus a buffer of at least one-half mile, where the free-phase CO2 is expected to stay through 2054 and five years after (p34).
mma_definition: Defined as identical to the AMA: the two unit boundaries plus a half-mile buffer, since the plume is expected to be held by the reservoir's geologic truncation limits (p6, p34-35).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Wellbores (especially legacy wells and drilling of new wells) and surface equipment are treated as the realistic pathways ('unlikely but possible'); shallow groundwater wells, faults/fractures, lateral movement, the confining seal and seismicity are all rated unlikely with low magnitude (p5, p36-39, p41, p46).
baseline_summary: No pre-injection environmental baseline. The baseline is ongoing operational data on injection well pressures and rates plus pattern performance; the plan may elect to collect ambient air data later. Reference gas values cited: 0.6% CO2 in the Cunningham before 1982 injection, 0.25% average in Hart wells sampled October 2023, and basin-wide published CO2 ranges, to be consulted if a leak is detected (p39, p46).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report with the mass balance (Equation RR-11) and any leakage events with estimated amounts; records kept at least three years; mechanical failures of surface casing or cement reported to the appropriate regulatory authority. No commitment to publish measurement data (p42, p45, p47, p50, p53).
notes: Figure pages (p10-12, 14-15, 17-19, 23-25, 27-29, 32-33, 37, 40) carry only captions; Figure 22 well map and the Appendix 1 well list (886 wellbores) are not in the text. Groundwater is contradictory: p36 commits to annual testing of one groundwater well, while p46 says USDW wells have not been monitored; coded as committed on the explicit 'will test' sentence. MIT frequency is annual or five-yearly depending on permitted rate, so coded multi_year. Reservoir pressure is listed as a monitoring provision, yet p30 says actual reservoir pressure was unavailable and the last measurement dates to Fox et al. (1988); hence mentioned_only. Visual inspection frequency is stated as 'weekly or daily' (p42), daily for surface equipment (p46), weekly in Table 4; coded weekly as the floor. Soil gas and RTS use permissive 'may elect'/'sometimes' language. No fresh CO2 has been received since 2022; implementation is expected in 2026 after approval and securing a new CO2 supply (p13, p50). No seismic surveys, personal or fixed gas detectors, InSAR or microseismic arrays are mentioned.

plan_title: Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan O'Neal Gas Unit Well No. 4
ama_definition: Set equal to the MMA: the circular area around the single injector covering the modeled stabilized plume plus a half-mile buffer, after checking that the plume five years past end of injection stays inside the 12-year plume plus buffer; a revised AMA/MMA is promised by 2037 (p48, p50).
mma_definition: A circle around the O'Neal No. 4 covering the modeled free-phase plume after 12 years of injection and 10 years of density drift (about 0.45 mi radius, 303 acres) plus a half-mile all-around buffer (p48).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Every pathway is rated low magnitude. Surface equipment is the only one rated 'possible' (during injection); existing wells (one plugged well penetrates the injection zone), faults (nearest interpreted fault about 4.25 mi away), the Pearsall confining zone, and natural/induced seismicity are all 'unlikely', with any vertical migration expected to be caught in a shallower gas reservoir (p52, p55, p61-62).
baseline_summary: Pre-injection baselines are planned: baseline readings of the fixed H2S/CO2 monitors during commissioning, an atmospheric CO2 concentration at the facility, soil gas samples near the one plugged penetrating well, and groundwater samples from water wells (pH, TDS, CO2, VOC), all estimated for Oct. 1, 2024 but tied to permit/EPA approval. Operational baseline of injection volumes and pressures is recorded at start of injection (p65, p72-73, p77).
reporting_summary: Annual Subpart RR report filed March 31 with the RR-12 mass balance; soil gas and groundwater lab results are included in the annual report only if they show a material variance from baseline; flare/blowdown emissions are reported under the facility's GHG reporting and Subpart W; records kept at least 3 years. No commitment to publish measurement data; MRV plan revisions to EPA within 180 days (p72-73, p75-77, p79-80).
notes: Class II permit was pending at submission; the plan says baseline data cannot be dated until the permit issues and the MRV plan will be implemented on EPA approval (p77). Figure-only pages (49, 51, 56-58, 60, 63, 66, 69, 71) and the appendices (81-82 are index pages only; forms, well lists not included). Annulus pressure is coded committed on a single sentence that implies monitoring without describing it (p67). Above-zone monitoring uses third-party-style producing gas wells; composition sampling frequency is not stated beyond 'regular' and 'monthly production statements', and whether Ozona operates these wells is not said. production_monitoring is not_found because this is not EOR (no CO2 produced, p75); the produced-gas CO2 checks are coded under above_zone_monitoring. Atmospheric CO2 is coded mentioned_only because only a one-time pre-operation baseline is promised and it may simply be the commissioning baseline of the fixed H2S/CO2 monitors (Table 10). Groundwater sampling: baseline on all wells but 'select wells' annually (p73). Minor inconsistencies: stabilized plume year given as 2047 (p16, p61) and 2062 (p26); TexNet station figure referenced as Figure 38 but is Figure 39 (p70-71). Monitoring commitment covers 12-year injection plus a 10-year post-injection period (p64).

plan_title: Petra Nova West Ranch Oil Field CO2 Monitoring, Reporting and Verification (MRV) Plan
ama_definition: The existing West Ranch 41-A/98-A (Consolidated) Unit boundary plus a half-mile buffer, to be expanded to cover any new unit formed for CO2 EOR within the Project Interval, plus the same buffer (p24-25).
mma_definition: The outermost boundary of all Frio reservoirs in the Project Interval that could be developed by CO2 EOR, set by oil-water contacts and structure, plus a half-mile buffer (p25-26).
leakage_pathways_rated_significant: Every pathway is rated low or highly unlikely. plan_title: Red Trail Energy Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan

Downhole gauges are 'NA' in the pre-injection column but a pre-injection pressure falloff test is planned, so reservoir_pressure baseline is marked unclear. InSAR and gravity are listed in the table only 'if feasible' pending a feasibility study, so coded mentioned_only per the weaker-level rule; a reader may view them as conditional on feasibility. plan_title: Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan, Rose Carbon Capture and Storage Facility, Jefferson County, Texas

plan_title: ExxonMobil Shute Creek Treating Facility Subpart RR Second Amended Monitoring, Reporting and Verification Plan

notes: The plan covers two different well groups: the AGI wells (acid gas disposal, 35-50% CO2 / 50-65% H2S) and the new SC 5-2 and SC 7-34 wells (99% CO2 disposal); 'acid_gas_disposal' was chosen for injection_purpose, but co2_disposal applies to the SC wells. Cover date is February 2025 while the Introduction calls it 'dated October 2024' (p5). Many figure pages (p17-19, 21-23, 31-35) are images with little or no text. Monitoring is almost entirely surface-based (DCS injection parameters, fixed H2S/CO2 detectors, personal monitors, visual rounds, annual MIT, smart pigging); there is no annulus pressure monitoring, observation well, above-zone, groundwater, soil gas or seismometer commitment. Visual inspections are daily at the AGI facility and weekly at all well sites, so 'weekly' was chosen as the row frequency. Passive seismic is coded conditional because the text only commits to consulting the ANSS catalogue if an event occurs, even though Table 5.1 lists it as a monitoring program (p43). The plan explicitly rejects an annual leak survey of components as unsafe-to-monitor and relies on continuous gas detectors instead (p47). 'Monitoring will occur for the duration of injection' (p43); no post-injection monitoring is described. Updated SC 7-34 reservoir properties and well logs are promised in the first annual report after that well starts (p15). Page citations were corrected after the independent check: the coder had cited printed page numbers, one less than the PDF page. Page references inside this notes field may still use printed numbers.

plan_title: EOG SPG Holdings, Inc. Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification Plan for SPG CO2 Bowie Facility, Montague County, TX

plan_title: Tundra SGS Subpart RR Monitoring, Reporting, and Verification (MRV) Plan

baseline_summary: A pre-injection baseline period of at least one year covering all four seasons: surface water, soil gas, shallow groundwater from selected domestic wells and a USGS Fox Hills well (sampled August 2021), formation water, saturation logs and casing inspection logs in injection and monitoring wells, a baseline 3D seismic survey, seismometer stations installed a year before injection, and an InSAR feasibility study (p16, p31-32, p36-37).

notes: No version or date printed on the cover. Much of the monitoring detail is incorporated by reference to Storage Facility Permit attachments (A1/A2 sections and appendices) that are not included in the text. The weekly 'Handheld CO2 Monitor' is coded under fixed_gas_detectors (scheduled handheld survey), not personal_gas_monitors or atmospheric_co2, because the plan does not call it atmospheric monitoring. Soil gas frequency 'three to four seasonal samples per year' was coded as quarterly. Groundwater sampling coded multi_year because the schedule becomes every 5 years after year 5. InSAR is listed as continuous in Table 4-1 but the text says a feasibility study will determine its application, so it is coded conditional. Phase 2 (Deadwood–Black Island, McCall-1 well) is contingent; the plan says no MRV modification is needed if pursued. A Class I disposal well (Freeman-1) into the Inyan Kara is planned on the same pad. Permanent DTS/DAS fiber is coded under cased_hole_logging, as in v1.3.
